summary: Clackamas County summit lookout about four miles from Mount Hood; USFS tower dated to the 1930s, now gone, with only concrete footings reported.

facts.design: Lookout tower on concrete footings, with a garage and storage shed around its base (1944 plans)
facts.status_note: Listed as gone or removed; the WyEast Blog reports concrete footings as the only remaining traces

access.note: Summit reached on foot by an unmarked old path that most Timberline Trail visitors walk past; a Northwest Forest Pass is needed to park at the trailheads

visit.trail_note: Hike from Lolo Pass or the Top Spur trailhead; hikes usually open mid-June to mid-November

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register dates the USFS tower to the 1930s and a photo is dated 1934. The WyEast Blog reads a 1911 map as showing an earlier lookout, probably a platform later replaced by a tower. A guide dates traces of a lookout to the 1940s. These can all be true of successive structures, but no source here gives a construction year for the standing tower.
The register gives 4,591 ft (1,399 m). Firelookout.com gives 5133 ft. The record keeps the register figure.
The WyEast Blog places the summit about four miles from Mount Hood's west face; Firelookout.com places it four miles northwest of Mount Hood. The register coordinates are used in the record.

notes_for_editor: Access was 'unknown' in the brief; filled as public because the summit path is open to hikers. No source gives a removal date or reason. Brief's conflict note ('They share a register number') could not be checked against the sources read. The firelookout.org list gives coordinates 45.39725, -121.74509, which differ from the register coordinates the record uses. Two other pages named Bald Mountain (Josephine County, NHLR US 480 in Klamath County) were not used. No staffing or fire history found.
